setup_steps: Open the paragraph style list and apply “Heading 1”.
Type “This is the first page of the chapter.”
Choose Insert > Footer > Default Page Style.
task.main_task: Insert the current chapter name into the footer
main_steps: In the Fields dialog, click the “Document” tab.
In the Format list, select “Chapter name”.

task.setup_task: (Setup) Create a footer with page number text
setup_steps: Choose Insert > Footer > Default Page Style.
task.main_task: Add a page count after the page number so the footer shows a Page X of Y format
main_steps: Click immediately after the page number field in the footer.

task.main_task: Insert an invisible user-defined variable field named ProLite with the value Lite
main_steps: Open the Insert menu and choose Field, then More Fields.
Click the Variables tab in the Fields dialog.
Select Set variable in the Type list.
Select Text in the Format list.
Click the Name box and type ProLite.
Click the Value box and type Lite.

title: Conditional text
path: Apply the condition to the content

task.setup_task: (Setup) Define the ProLite variable with the value Lite
setup_steps: Open the Insert menu and choose Field > More Fields.
In the Fields dialog, click the Variables tab.
In the Type list, select Set variable.
Click the Name box and type ProLite.
Click the Value box and type Lite.
task.main_task: Insert conditional text that displays Great Product Lite
main_steps: Click at the end of the variable field in the document.
Open the Insert menu and choose Field > More Fields.
In the Fields dialog, click the Functions tab.
In the Type list, select Conditional text.
Click the Condition box and type ProLite EQ "Lite".
Click the Then box and type Great Product Lite.
Click the Else box and type Great Product Pro.

task.setup_task: (Setup) Define the ProLite variable with the value Lite
setup_steps: Open the Insert menu and choose Field > More Fields.
In the Fields dialog, click the Variables tab.
In the Type list, select Set variable.
Click the Name box and type ProLite.
Click the Value box and type Lite.
task.main_task: Insert hidden text and make it visible for editing
main_steps: Click at the end of the variable field in the document.
Open the Insert menu and choose Field > More Fields.
In the Fields dialog, click the Functions tab.
In the Type list, select Hidden text.
Click the Condition box and type ProLite EQ "Lite".
Click the Hidden text box and type , and six color choices.
Open the Tools menu and choose Options.
In the Options dialog, open LibreOffice Writer and click View.
Select the Hidden text option in Display fields.

title: Hidden paragraphs
path: Apply the condition to the content

task.setup_task: (Setup) Create a paragraph that can be turned into a hidden paragraph
setup_steps: Type "This paragraph is hidden when the condition is true."
task.main_task: Apply a hidden paragraph condition to the paragraph
main_steps: Select "Hidden Paragraph" in the Type list.

task.setup_task: (Setup) Create text for a conditional section
setup_steps: Type "Section text to be hidden when the condition is true."
task.main_task: Create a hidden section from the selected text
main_steps: In the Insert Section dialog, go to the "Section" tab.
Type "Section1" in the section name field.

title: Change the value of the variable
path: Change the value of the variable

task.setup_task: (Setup) Create a variable field with the value Lite
setup_steps: Open the Insert menu and click Field.
Select Set variable in the Type list.
Type ProLite in the Name box.
Type Lite in the Value box.
task.main_task: Change the ProLite variable field value from Lite to Pro
main_steps: Click immediately in front of the inserted variable field in the document.
In the Edit Fields dialog, click the Value box.
Press Ctrl+A in the Value box.
Click the check mark button or press Enter.

task.main_task: Insert an image placeholder field that shows the placeholder text and help tip text
main_steps: Open the Insert menu and click Field.
Select Placeholder in the Type list.
Select Image in the Format list.

task.main_task: Show the TSCP Classification toolbar in Writer
main_steps: Click View in the menu bar.

task.main_task: Open the document properties window to the Custom Properties tab after enabling document classification tools
main_steps: Click View in the menu bar.
Click File in the menu bar.

task.main_task: Show the TSCP Classification toolbar in Writer
Open the document properties custom properties tab after enabling document classification tools

title: User data
path: Choosing options for all of LibreOffice

task.main_task: Enter user information in LibreOffice user data and turn off using it for document properties
main_steps: Click Tools in the menu bar.
In the left pane, expand LibreOffice.
Click the First name field and type "Alex".
Click the Last name field and type "Morgan".
Click the Initials field and type "AM".
Click the Company field and type "Northwind Press".
Clear the checkbox labeled "Use data for document properties".

task.main_task: Enable both print warning options in LibreOffice print settings
main_steps: Click Tools in the menu bar.
In the left pane, expand LibreOffice.
In the Warnings section, select the checkbox labeled "Paper size".
In the Warnings section, select the checkbox labeled "Paper orientation".

title: Paths options
path: Choosing options for all of LibreOffice

task.main_task: Turn on a paper size warning for printing options
main_steps: In the Options dialog, select LibreOffice.
In the Warnings section, select the Paper size checkbox.

task.main_task: Show text boundaries and change their display color in application colors
main_steps: In the Options dialog, select LibreOffice.
In the list of interface elements, find Text boundaries.
Select the checkbox in the On column for Text boundaries.
Click the color drop-down for Text boundaries.
Select a color from the list.

title: Application colors
path: Choosing options for all of LibreOffice

task.main_task: Show text boundaries in Writer using Application Colors options
main_steps: In the Options dialog, click LibreOffice > Application Colors.
In the Custom Colors list, find Text boundaries.
Select the checkbox in the On column for Text boundaries.

task.main_task: Change the color of text boundaries and save it as a color scheme
main_steps: In the Options dialog, click LibreOffice > Application Colors.
In the Custom Colors list, find Text boundaries.
Select the checkbox in the On column for Text boundaries.
Open the Color setting drop-down for Text boundaries.
Type BoundaryBlue in the Scheme box.
Click OK in the scheme dialog.
Click OK in the Options dialog.

title: General
path: Choosing options for loading and saving documents

task.main_task: Enable backup creation and set AutoRecovery to save every 10 minutes in Load/Save General options
main_steps: In the left pane, click the expansion control next to Load/Save.
Ensure the checkbox for Save AutoRecovery information every is selected.
Click the minutes field and enter 10.
Select the checkbox Always create backup copy.

task.main_task: Change the default text document save format to Word 2007–365 and set the ODF version to 1.2 Extended
main_steps: In the left pane, click the expansion control next to Load/Save.
In Default File Format and ODF Settings, open the ODF format version list.
Verify Document type is Text document.
Open the Always save as list.

task.setup_task: (Setup) Insert a drawing object to prepare for testing helplines while moving
setup_steps: Click and drag in the document to draw a rectangle near the upper-left area of the page.
task.main_task: Enable Helplines While Moving and move the rectangle so the guide lines appear across the page
main_steps: In the left pane, expand LibreOffice Writer if needed.
Select the Helplines While Moving checkbox.
Click the rectangle to select it.
Drag the rectangle to a different position on the page.

task.setup_task: (Setup) Insert an image to prepare for changing Writer view display options
setup_steps: Select any available image file and confirm the insertion so the image appears in the document.
task.main_task: Hide images and objects in Writer so the inserted image is no longer shown in the document view
main_steps: In the left pane, expand LibreOffice Writer if needed.
Clear the Images and objects checkbox.

task.main_task: Enable Writer grid snapping and make the grid visible with specific spacing values
main_steps: Open the Tools menu and choose Options.
In the Options dialog, expand LibreOffice Writer if needed and click Grid.
In Horizontal under Resolution, enter 0.50 cm.
In Vertical under Resolution, enter 0.10 cm.

task.main_task: Change the default image anchor in Writer to To Character
main_steps: Open the Tools menu and choose Options.
In the Options dialog, expand LibreOffice Writer if needed and click Formatting Aids.

task.main_task: Change the basic Western font settings for Writer defaults
main_steps: Open the Tools menu and choose Options.
In the Options dialog, expand LibreOffice Writer.
Open the Heading font drop-down and select Liberation Serif.
Open the Heading size drop-down and select 14 pt.
Open the Default font drop-down and select Liberation Serif.
Open the Default size drop-down and select 11 pt.

task.main_task: Reset Writer basic Western font settings to the installed defaults
main_steps: Open the Tools menu and choose Options.
In the Options dialog, expand LibreOffice Writer.

task.main_task: Change Writer’s default print settings to print only right pages and print text in black
main_steps: In the Options dialog, expand LibreOffice Writer if needed.
Click the checkbox for Print text in black.
Click the checkbox for Left pages to clear it.

task.main_task: Change Writer’s default print settings so comments print at the end of the document and brochure printing is enabled
main_steps: In the Options dialog, expand LibreOffice Writer if needed.
In the Comments section, select End of document.
In the Pages section, click the checkbox for Brochure.

task.main_task: Set Writer comparison options to compare by character and store the random number when changing the document
main_steps: Open the Tools menu and select Options.
In the Options window, expand LibreOffice Writer.
Select the By character option in the Compare Documents section.
Check Store it when changing the document in the Random number to improve accuracy of document comparison section.

task.main_task: Change the comparison options to compare by word and take the random number into account when comparing
main_steps: Open the Tools menu and select Options.
In the Options window, expand LibreOffice Writer.
Select the By word option in the Compare Documents section.
Check Take it into account when comparing in the Random number to improve accuracy of document comparison section.

task.setup_task: (Setup) Create an image object in the document for testing automatic captions
setup_steps: Select any available image file and confirm the insertion.
task.main_task: Enable automatic captions for Writer images and set the caption category to Figure
main_steps: In the options tree, expand LibreOffice Writer.
In the list of objects, click LibreOffice Writer Image.
Select the checkbox for LibreOffice Writer Image if it is not already selected.
Replace the current text with Figure.

task.setup_task: (Setup) Create a table in the document for testing automatic table captions
setup_steps: Set the number of columns to 2.
Set the number of rows to 2.
task.main_task: Enable automatic captions for Writer tables and set the caption position below the table
main_steps: In the options tree, expand LibreOffice Writer.
In the list of objects, click LibreOffice Writer Table.
Select the checkbox for LibreOffice Writer Table if it is not already selected.

task.main_task: Open the online dictionaries page from Writer
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.

task.main_task: Open the Language Settings - Languages options page and enable document-only language settings
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
In the left pane, expand Language Settings.
On the right side, check For the current document only.

title: Change some locale and language settings
path: Change some locale and language settings

task.main_task: Change the language settings so they apply only to the current document and ignore the system input language
main_steps: In the left pane, expand Language Settings.
On the right side, check For the current document only.

task.main_task: Enable support for Asian languages and complex text layout languages in Writer options
main_steps: In the left pane, expand Language Settings.
In the Default Languages for Documents section, check Asian.
In the Default Languages for Documents section, check Complex text layout.

task.main_task: Create a custom user-defined dictionary named “technical” in the writing aids settings
main_steps: In the Options dialog, expand Language Settings.
In the User-defined Dictionaries section, click New.
Type technical in the dictionary name field.
Confirm the dialog to create the dictionary.
Verify that “technical” appears in the User-defined Dictionaries list.
Click OK to close the Options dialog.

task.main_task: Open English sentence checking options from Extension Manager and enable an additional grammar check
main_steps: In the list of extensions, select English spelling dictionaries.
In the English Sentence Checking options, select one unchecked optional feature.

task.main_task: Enable an additional English sentence-checking option in the English spelling dictionaries extension
main_steps: In the Extension Manager dialog, select English spelling dictionaries.
In the English Sentence Checking options, check one unchecked optional feature.

task.main_task: Add the “About LibreOffice” command to the File menu in Writer
main_steps: In the Customize dialog, click the Menus tab.
Open the Scope drop-down and select LibreOffice Writer.
Open the Target drop-down and select File.
In the Available Commands list, click About LibreOffice.
Click the large right arrow to add it to the File menu.

task.main_task: Create a new menu named Favorites and move it upward in the menu order
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
Click the button next to Target.
Type Favorites in the Menu name box.
Click the up arrow once in the New Menu dialog.

task.main_task: Add a command to an existing toolbar
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
Open the Scope drop-down list and choose Writer.
Open the Target drop-down list and select Standard.
Click a command in the Available Commands list.
Click the large right arrow to add it to the Assigned Commands list.

task.main_task: Create a new toolbar named PracticeBar saved for Writer
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
Click the button next to the Target drop-down.
In the Name dialog, type PracticeBar.

task.setup_task: Create a new toolbar to customize
setup_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
Click the button next to the Target drop-down.
In the Name dialog, type IconPractice.
task.main_task: Open the Change Icon dialog for the IconPractice toolbar and assign an icon to a selected command
main_steps: In the Available Commands list, click a command that shows an icon in the list.
Click the right-arrow button to add the selected command to the Assigned Commands list.
In the Assigned Commands list, click the command you added.
In the Change Icon dialog, click the first icon in the icon grid.

task.main_task: Switch Writer to the Tabbed user interface and hide one Notebookbar command
main_steps: In the Assigned Commands list, expand File Tab | File if it is collapsed.

task.main_task: Assign a new keyboard shortcut to the Bold function in Writer
main_steps: Set the shortcut assignment scope to Writer only.
Select Ctrl+Alt+B in the Shortcut Keys list.

task.main_task: Open the Extension Manager and start checking for extension updates
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
In the Extension Manager dialog, click Check for Updates.

task.main_task: Open the Customize dialog and reset keyboard shortcuts to their default values
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
In the Customize dialog, click the Keyboard tab.

task.main_task: Open the Extension Manager and start checking for extension updates
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
In the Extension Manager dialog, click Check for Updates.

task.main_task: Open the Extension Manager and open the online extensions page
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
In the Extension Manager dialog, click Get more extensions online.

task.main_task: Disable an installed extension in the Extension Manager so its button changes to Enable
main_steps: Click an extension listed under Installed for current user or Installed for all users.

task.main_task: Remove an installed extension from the Extension Manager
main_steps: Click an extension listed under Installed for current user or Installed for all users.

task.setup_task: Create a drawing object that can be used to open the Area dialog
setup_steps: Click and drag in the document to draw a rectangle.
task.main_task: Add a custom color to a palette by entering Hex notation
main_steps: Open the Palette drop-down and select standard.
Click the Hex field under New.

task.setup_task: Create a drawing object that can be used to open the Area dialog
setup_steps: Click and drag in the document to draw a rectangle.
task.main_task: Define a new custom color by using the Pick a Color dialog and save it to a palette
main_steps: Open the Palette drop-down and select standard.
Click the Hex # field in the Pick a Color dialog.
